clinical_summary.course_summary: The patient is a 25-year-old male with a medical history of obesity. He presented to the hospital with a three-day history of high-grade fever with chills, severe headache, nausea, right hypochondriac pain, and generalized weakness. Previous outpatient treatment from a general practitioner on 06/01/2026 failed to relieve these symptoms. Upon admission on 09/01/2026, clinical assessment revealed severe hypotension (BP 90/50 mmHg), tachycardia (104/min), and dehydration. Diagnostic investigations confirmed Typhoid fever through positive IgG and IgM antibodies. Laboratory results showed systemic inflammation and hepatic involvement, with an initial CRP of 275 and elevated liver enzymes (SGOT 56, SGPT 88). The CRP levels peaked at 299 on 10/01/2026. Treatment consisted of intravenous fluids, antibiotics (Inj. Cefotroy SB Forte), proton pump inhibitors, and antiemetics. Recurrent high-grade fever spikes were managed with Inj. Neomol, with a maximum recorded temperature of 103.2°F. During the four-day hospitalization, vitals trended toward stabilization. By 13/01/2026, the patient’s blood pressure improved to 120/80 mmHg, and the CRP level reduced significantly to 48. The patient was discharged in a vitally and hemodynamically stable condition. Post-discharge care instructions included physical rest, a healthy diet, and a five-day course of oral medications: Tab. Pexime (200mg), Tab. Calpol (650mg), and Tab. N B D3. A follow-up assessment was advised after 5 days.
